lean.statement:
let F := fun (n : ℕ+) (β lam : {r : ℝ // 0 < r}) (y : ℝ) ↦
  (n : ℝ) * (β : ℝ) ^ 2 / (lam : ℝ) *
    ∫ s in (0 : ℝ)..((lam : ℝ) * y / ((n : ℝ) * (β : ℝ))),
      expNegInvGlue (2 - |s|) /
        (expNegInvGlue (2 - |s|) + expNegInvGlue (|s| - 1))
;
∀ {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω]
    (P : Measure Ω) (n : ℕ+) (β lam : {r : ℝ // 0 < r}) {Y : Ω → ℝ}
    (v : ℝ≥0) (hY : ProbabilityTheory.HasLaw Y (ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 v) P)
    {a : ℝ} (ha : a ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1),
    Integrable (fun ω ↦ Real.exp (-a * F n β lam (Y ω))) P ∧
      (∫ ω, Real.exp (-a * F n β lam (Y ω)) ∂P) ≤
        Real.exp ((β : ℝ) ^ 2 * ProbabilityTheory.variance Y P / 2)
approved_definition_context: ℕ+ denotes positive natural numbers, coerced to real numbers where displayed. The subtype {r : ℝ // 0 < r} consists of strictly positive reals with their positivity proofs.
expNegInvGlue t is 0 for t ≤ 0 and exp(-1/t) for t > 0. The displayed interval integral uses real Lebesgue measure and oriented endpoints.
HasLaw Y μ P means AEMeasurable Y P and Measure.map Y P = μ. gaussianReal m v is the Gaussian probability law with mean m and variance v, with zero variance giving the Dirac law at m.

Integrable f P asserts a.e. strong measurability and finite integral of the norm; the integral is the real Bochner integral. variance Y P is real-valued variance; for a Gaussian law it is finite and equals the variance parameter.
